Sunrise and sunset can have their own smoothing. Hysteresis is how far the light may drift before the exposure starts to move; smoothness is how long the exposure takes to reach its full rate of change. Larger values make the exposure change more gently but follow the light more slowly.

Drag ISO, aperture and shutter speed up or down with the ⇅ handle on the left. The exposure moves the top one first. When the top one reaches its limit the middle one moves, and when that reaches its limit the bottom one moves.
The exposure does not move while the light stays within this band (± half of it) around the target. A wider band ignores small flickers in the light but reacts more slowly to real changes.

How long the exposure takes to go from not moving to its full rate of change. A longer time eases the start and end of each change and reduces flicker in the video, but lags slightly behind fast changes such as passing clouds.
